EXC-2028 Keep comment lines out of Implementation counts

TL;DR

  • When a hunk changes code and comments or docstrings together, its comment and docstring lines count toward Docs & Comments, so Implementation's numbers count only real code.
  • The files stay listed under Implementation. Docs & Comments gets one "implementation comments / docstrings" item that sums those lines and lists them per file.
  • The Documentation section is renamed "Docs & Comments".

Problem / Motivation

The docstring rule judges whole hunks: a hunk moves to Documentation only when every line it changes is a comment or docstring. A hunk that edits a function and its docstring together, as when a Python change adds a parameter and documents it, counts entirely as Implementation, docstring lines included. Implementation's numbers then overstate how much code changed. Implementation lines changed should be "PURELY for the actual lines of real code changed, not documentation comments and strings and whatnot."

Expected Outcome

  • Implementation's pill, section total, and file rows count only changed code lines.
  • The comment and docstring lines taken out of Implementation count in the Docs & Comments pill and section total.
  • Their files are not listed in Docs & Comments and are not marked Partial, because listing them "would just be distracting" and "the numbers are what matters". Docs & Comments instead shows "a single phantom item that doesn't link to anything in particular", labeled along the lines of "implementation comments / docstrings". Hovering or focusing it shows which files changed comment or docstring lines, and how many in each.

Acceptance Criteria

  • ☐ In a file whose path section is Implementation, a hunk that changes both code and comment or docstring lines counts its code lines toward Implementation and its comment and docstring lines toward Docs & Comments.
  • ☐ This holds for every syntax the comment scan supports (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript/Rust, Go, Lua), and line comments (#, //, --) count the same as docstrings and block comments.
  • ☐ Changed blank lines in a mixed hunk count toward Implementation, as do lines with both code and a trailing comment (x = 1 # note).
  • ☐ The file's Implementation row, Implementation's section total, and the Implementation pill exclude the moved lines. A row can then differ from GitHub's per-file count and from the hunks its click reveals.
  • ☐ Docs & Comments shows one phantom item whenever at least one line was moved, even when it is the section's only entry. Its count is the sum across files, and clicking it reveals nothing.
  • ☐ Hovering or keyboard-focusing the phantom item lists each contributing file with the comment lines it adds and removes.
  • ☐ The phantom item isn't a file: it's left out of Docs & Comments' file and Viewed counts, and alt-click doesn't mark anything Viewed.
  • ☐ Comment lines from mixed hunks always go to the phantom item, even when the file already has a Docs & Comments entry from comment-only hunks. That entry still counts only the hunks its click reveals.
  • ☐ The breakout's pills still add up to GitHub's total, for added and for removed lines.
  • ☐ Intent cached before this change never shows the old numbers.
  • ☐ The section's label and description read "Docs & Comments", and CONTEXT.md (including a term for the phantom item), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, and the README match.
  • ☐ Unit tests cover the line split for each supported syntax, including a trailing comment, a block comment whose opener is above the hunk, and a Python multi-line string that isn't a docstring.
  • ☐ gh-prism-sandbox has a PR for each supported comment syntax (Python, C-like, Go, Lua), and gh-prism's numbers match each PR's counts, which are known in advance. Together the PRs cover a mixed hunk, a file with both a comment-only hunk and a mixed hunk, and a mixed hunk in a test file.

Constraints

  • Only hunks that stay in Implementation are split by line, because the issue targets Implementation's numbers. A mixed hunk in a Tests or Config file keeps all its lines in that section.
  • Placement doesn't change: files and hunks land where they do today, and only the line counts move.
  • A line the comment scan can't confirm is a comment counts as Implementation. The scan itself is out of scope.
  • Path-only views (intent unreadable, or commit-filtered) keep counting by path, so their Implementation numbers include comment lines.
  • The phantom item's file list renders paths as text, the same way the sidebar does.
  • The section's key stays docs.
  • There is no setting to turn this off.
